principles: Benchmark proves claim-admissibility control effectiveness, not quantum truth.
All Quantum M4-M5 outputs stay local, read-only, diagnostic-only, and non-gate evidence.
Supported and failure-injection cases must be deterministic and reviewer-readable.
Boundary booleans for theory, hardware, solver improvement, production, and Authority remain false.
Prefer a minimal Quantum-specific slice over generic framework gate integration.
drivers: M0-M3 evaluator and gate-policy projection already exist and should be reused rather than duplicated.
INIT reviewers require A1-A4 semantics to be explicit before REVIEW.
High-risk auto-elevation from the word production requires clear no-production preMortem and evidence.

options.name: docs-only M4-M5 closeout
cons: Does not actually complete benchmark/report runtime capability

options.name: local deterministic benchmark and report commands
pros: Completes M4-M5 as runnable local diagnostics

options.name: generic lifecycle gate-policy adapter plus benchmark
cons: Risks weakening or duplicating lifecycle gates
Conflates Quantum local completion with generic framework M4

chosen: local deterministic benchmark and report commands
rationale: This option completes the remaining Quantum local diagnostic milestones with concrete runnable evidence while preserving all proof-or-stop boundaries and avoiding generic lifecycle gate integration scope creep.

preMortem.trigger: Benchmark emits opaque A1/A2 labels without docs or stable case meaning
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers cannot tell whether M4 is complete or just label-driven
preMortem.mitigation: Define A1-A4 in code and docs as supported-control cases with explicit expected decisions.

preMortem.scenario: Benchmark report is mistaken for production or Authority proof
preMortem.trigger: Report wording uses completion language without boundary qualifiers
preMortem.consequence: Host or user may overclaim quantum readiness or release readiness
preMortem.mitigation: Every report includes diagnosticOnly=true, gateEvidence=false, productionClaim=false, authorityClaim=false, and explicit limitations.

preMortem.scenario: Failure injections pass for the wrong reason
preMortem.trigger: B1-B15 expected stop/degrade assertions only check non-advance without validating reason categories
preMortem.consequence: The harness hides regressions in stale/mismatch/boundary handling
preMortem.mitigation: Each injected case records expected decision and required reason prefix; smoke asserts exact category coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Generic framework M4 gets accidentally claimed complete
preMortem.trigger: Docs say M4/M5 implemented without saying local Quantum diagnostic slice
preMortem.consequence: Framework roadmap becomes false and future gate adapter work is obscured
preMortem.mitigation: Docs explicitly distinguish Quantum local M4-M5 from generic framework gate-policy adapter work.
